summary: Doaktown Lookout Station in Northumberland County, named in 1937 and 1948 annual reports through telephone-line work; no source gives its build date or present state.

facts.agency: New Brunswick Department of Lands and Mines (annual reports, as quoted on Canada Lookouts)

events.note: Part of the telephone line from Doaktown to the Doaktown Lookout Station was rebuilt on a more satisfactory location, with warden labour
Six miles of metallic circuit telephone line on poles connected the Doaktown tower to the Doaktown exchange; the old line was dismantled

evidence.supports: The 1937 report names the Doaktown Lookout Station in Northumberland County
evidence.quote: 1937: "In Northumberland County part of the telephone line from Doaktown to Doaktown Lookout Station was rebuilt

evidence.supports: The telephone line was changed to a more satisfactory location, using warden labour where possible
evidence.quote: being changed to a more satisfactory location, warden labour being used where possible

evidence.supports: The 1948 line connected the Doaktown tower to the Doaktown exchange, via the New Betts Mills Brook Settlement Road and the Grand Lake Road
evidence.quote: 1948: "Six miles of metallic circuit telephone line on poles was erected connecting Doaktown tower, via the New Betts Mills Brook Settlement Road and the Grand Lake Road, to Doaktown exchange

evidence.supports: The report expected good telephone service for the tower, and the old line was dismantled
evidence.quote: This will give this tower good telephone service in future. The old line, which was badly in need of repair, was dismantled

evidence.supports: The 1937 entry comes from the 77th annual report
evidence.quote: 77th Annual report of the Department of Lands and Mines

evidence.supports: The 1948 entry comes from the 112th annual report
evidence.quote: 112th Annual Report of the Department of Lands and Mines

notes_for_editor: One source: Canada Lookouts quoting the 77th (1937) and 112th (1948) annual reports of the Department of Lands and Mines. Both entries concern a telephone line, not the tower itself. No source gives a build date, staffing, fate or present condition for the tower. The story treats the 1937 Doaktown Lookout Station and the 1948 Doaktown tower as one site; the two reports appear to describe the same place but neither says so outright. Two WebSearch calls found no other Doaktown lookout record, and the cached Doaktown Wikipedia article has no lookout or tower mention in its text. The brief's coordinates (46.503, -66.1534) were not checked against a source. The brief's status, access and kind are left as unknown because no source supports a value. The 77th report number does not fit the 112th for 1948 (35 reports in 11 years), so the 1937 label or the report number may be wrong on the source; the story follows the page as printed. Confidence is low; the short story reflects thin evidence, not a cut.
